system_prompt:
You are a careful analytics engineer proposing dbt data tests for ONE model.

You receive the model SQL, its yml (with column descriptions), aggregate-only column
profiles, the tests that already exist, and the other models you may reference.

Rules:
- Allowed test types: not_null, unique, accepted_values, relationships, singular_sql. Nothing else.
- Ground every proposal in evidence: cite the specific statistic (e.g. "null_pct=0.0",
  "all_distinct=true", "min=0") and/or the yml description or SQL that implies the rule.
- accepted_values: only for columns whose profile has values_complete=true; list EXACTLY those
  values (same spelling, accents and case). Never invent values.
- relationships: config {"to": "ref('<model>')", "field": "<column>"}, only to models and
  columns listed in available_models.
- singular_sql: config {"slug": "short_snake_case_name", "sql": "..."}. The SQL must be a
  single SELECT (or WITH ... SELECT) that returns the rows that VIOLATE the rule, reads the model via
  {{ ref('<this model>') }}, and has no semicolon. Use these for cross-column invariants.
- Do not duplicate tests that already exist. Prefer a focused list of valuable tests over an
  exhaustive one (aim for 8-20). Skip columns where a test would be trivial or meaningless.
- You may propose a rule that the statistics cannot fully confirm if the descriptions or SQL
  clearly imply it; every proposal is validated against the real data before a human sees it.
- Set "column" to null for singular_sql tests that span columns.
- Boolean flag columns whose true-count (or false-count) is small but non-zero relative to the row
  count are known-defect indicators: the data producer is marking rows it knows are problematic.
  For each such column, propose a monitoring test with "severity": "warn" that fails when flagged
  rows exist, so the defect is tracked instead of silently ignored.
Return your answer ONLY by calling the submit_proposals tool.

payload_sent.model_sql:
{{ config(materialized='table') }}  {# table, not view: md5 and window functions over 3.2M rows would be recomputed by every downstream query #}

-- Staging model: 1:1 with raw.requetes311 (no rows removed).
-- Renames French columns to English, casts types, normalizes text, and adds
-- row-level flags describing known data quality issues (see docs/profiling.md).

{% set source_columns = adapter.get_columns_in_relation(source('raw', 'requetes311')) %}

with source as (

    select * from {{ source('raw', 'requetes311') }}

),

-- Step 1: fingerprint every row using the RAW (untouched) values.
-- md5() over all columns gives identical rows an identical hash.
-- coalesce(..., '<null>') matters: concat_ws silently skips NULLs, which would let
-- (a, NULL, b) and (a, b, NULL) collide. The '|' delimiter prevents ('ab','c') = ('a','bc').
fingerprinted as (

    select
        *,
        md5(concat_ws('|',
            {%- for col in source_columns %}
            coalesce("{{ col.name }}", '<null>'){{ "," if not loop.last }}
            {%- endfor %}
        )) as row_hash
    from source

),

-- Step 2: window functions over each group of identical rows.
--   count(*) over (partition by row_hash)  -> size of the group (1 = not duplicated)
--   row_number() over (partition by row_hash) -> 1, 2, 3... inside the group
-- Window functions keep every row (unlike GROUP BY, which would collapse them).
-- Rows in a group are identical, so the order within it is irrelevant: the set of
-- (row_hash, row_number) pairs is the same on every run, which keeps the key deterministic.
numbered as (

    select
        *,
        count(*)     over (partition by row_hash) as duplicate_group_size,
        row_number() over (partition by row_hash order by row_hash) as duplicate_row_number
    from fingerprinted

),

cleaned as (

    select
        -- Surrogate key: unique even for exact duplicates thanks to the row number.
        md5(row_hash || '|' || duplicate_row_number::varchar) as contact_sk,

        -- nullif(trim(x), ''): trim whitespace, and turn blank strings into real NULLs
        -- so "empty" is represented one way only.
        nullif(trim("ID_UNIQUE"), '')                  as request_id,
        nullif(trim("NATURE"), '')                     as contact_nature,

        -- Explicit casing fixes only; French text is never blanket-lower()ed because
        -- that would break proper nouns ("Île", "Saint-Laurent"). Add new variants here.
        case nullif(trim("ACTI_NOM"), '')
            when 'Soutien aux Élus' then 'Soutien aux élus'
            when 'soutien aux élus' then 'Soutien aux élus'
            else nullif(trim("ACTI_NOM"), '')
        end                                            as activity_name,

        nullif(trim("TYPE_LIEU_INTERV"), '')           as location_type,
        nullif(trim("RUE"), '')                        as street,
        nullif(trim("RUE_INTERSECTION1"), '')          as cross_street_1,
        nullif(trim("RUE_INTERSECTION2"), '')          as cross_street_2,

        -- Source stores '0'/'1' as text; compare to '1' to get a true boolean.
        ("LOC_ERREUR_GDT" = '1')                       as has_geocoding_error,

        -- The two borough columns use different separators ("A - B" vs "A-B").
        -- Standardize both to "A-B" so they can be compared and joined.
        replace(nullif(trim("ARRONDISSEMENT"), ''), ' - ', '-')     as borough,
        replace(nullif(trim("ARRONDISSEMENT_GEO"), ''), ' - ', '-') as borough_geo,

        -- Postal codes: strip spaces, then uppercase ('H1Y2m5' -> 'H1Y2M5').
        upper(replace(nullif(trim("LIN_CODE_POSTAL"), ''), ' ', '')) as postal_code,

        -- Source timestamps are ISO text with no timezone: America/Montreal local time.
        -- TIMESTAMP (not TIMESTAMPTZ) keeps them as-is. A plain cast fails loudly on bad
        -- values, which is what we want in staging.
        cast("DDS_DATE_CREATION" as timestamp)         as created_at,
        cast("DATE_DERNIER_STATUT" as timestamp)       as last_status_at,

        nullif(trim("PROVENANCE_ORIGINALE"), '')       as original_channel,

        -- PROVENANCE_* look like 0/1 flags but hold counts (max 60): how many times the
        -- same request was reported through each channel. Hence the *_contact_count names.
        cast("PROVENANCE_TELEPHONE" as integer)        as phone_contact_count,
        cast("PROVENANCE_COURRIEL" as integer)         as email_contact_count,
        cast("PROVENANCE_PERSONNE" as integer)         as in_person_contact_count,
        cast("PROVENANCE_COURRIER" as integer)         as mail_contact_count,
        cast("PROVENANCE_TELECOPIEUR" as integer)      as fax_contact_count,
        cast("PROVENANCE_INSTANCE" as integer)         as council_contact_count,
        cast("PROVENANCE_MOBILE" as integer)           as mobile_app_contact_count,
        cast("PROVENANCE_MEDIASOCIAUX" as integer)     as social_media_contact_count,
        cast("PROVENANCE_SITEINTERNET" as integer)     as website_contact_count,

        nullif(trim("UNITE_RESP_PARENT"), '')          as responsible_unit,

        cast("LOC_LONG" as double)                     as longitude,
        cast("LOC_LAT" as double)                      as latitude,
        cast("LOC_X" as double)                        as mtm_x,
        cast("LOC_Y" as double)                        as mtm_y,

        nullif(trim("DERNIER_STATUT"), '')             as last_status,

        duplicate_group_size,
        row_hash

    from numbered

),

final as (

    select
        *,

        -- Request ID anatomy: '22-105694-A' = year prefix, number, optional letter suffix.
        -- regexp_replace removes a trailing '-<letter>'; the '$' anchors to end of string,
        -- so '22-1' (a short ID, not a suffix) is left intact.
        regexp_replace(request_id, '-[A-Z]$', '')      as request_base_id,

        -- regexp_extract(..., group 1) returns just the captured letter, or '' if no match.
        nullif(regexp_extract(request_id, '-([A-Z])$', 1), '') as request_id_suffix,

        -- Data starts in 2022, so '20-'/'21-' prefixes are suspicious. coalesce(..., false):
        -- a NULL request_id makes LIKE return NULL, but a flag should be strictly true/false.
        coalesce(request_id like '20-%' or request_id like '21-%', false) as is_unexpected_id_prefix,

        -- Borough columns disagree. Both must be present: comparing with NULL yields NULL,
        -- and a missing value is not a "mismatch".
        coalesce(borough is not null and borough_geo is not null and borough <> borough_geo, false)
                                                       as borough_mismatch,

        -- Placeholder values in the borough column that are not real boroughs.
        coalesce(borough in ('Ville de Montréal', 'Extérieur de Montréal'), false)
                                                       as is_non_borough_value,

        duplicate_group_size > 1                       as is_exact_duplicate

    from cleaned

)

select
    contact_sk,
    request_id,
    request_base_id,
    request_id_suffix,
    is_unexpected_id_prefix,
    contact_nature,
    activity_name,
    created_at,
    last_status_at,
    last_status,
    original_channel,
    phone_contact_count,
    email_contact_count,
    in_person_contact_count,
    mail_contact_count,
    fax_contact_count,
    council_contact_count,
    mobile_app_contact_count,
    social_media_contact_count,
    website_contact_count,
    responsible_unit,
    location_type,
    street,
    cross_street_1,
    cross_street_2,
    postal_code,
    borough,
    borough_geo,
    borough_mismatch,
    is_non_borough_value,
    longitude,
    latitude,
    mtm_x,
    mtm_y,
    has_geocoding_error,
    is_exact_duplicate
from final
payload_sent.model_yml:
version: 2

models:
  - name: stg_311__contacts
    description: >
      Staging view over raw.requetes311, 1:1 with the source (no rows removed). English
      snake_case names, typed columns, trimmed text, standardized boroughs and postal codes,
      and row-level data quality flags. All timestamps are Montreal local time
      (America/Montreal) stored as TIMESTAMP without timezone.
      Column mapping (source -> staging): ID_UNIQUE -> request_id; NATURE -> contact_nature;
      ACTI_NOM -> activity_name; TYPE_LIEU_INTERV -> location_type; RUE -> street;
      RUE_INTERSECTION1 -> cross_street_1; RUE_INTERSECTION2 -> cross_street_2;
      LOC_ERREUR_GDT -> has_geocoding_error; ARRONDISSEMENT -> borough;
      ARRONDISSEMENT_GEO -> borough_geo; LIN_CODE_POSTAL -> postal_code;
      DDS_DATE_CREATION -> created_at; PROVENANCE_ORIGINALE -> original_channel;
      PROVENANCE_TELEPHONE -> phone_contact_count; PROVENANCE_COURRIEL -> email_contact_count;
      PROVENANCE_PERSONNE -> in_person_contact_count; PROVENANCE_COURRIER -> mail_contact_count;
      PROVENANCE_TELECOPIEUR -> fax_contact_count; PROVENANCE_INSTANCE -> council_contact_count;
      PROVENANCE_MOBILE -> mobile_app_contact_count; PROVENANCE_MEDIASOCIAUX -> social_media_contact_count;
      PROVENANCE_SITEINTERNET -> website_contact_count; UNITE_RESP_PARENT -> responsible_unit;
      LOC_LONG -> longitude; LOC_LAT -> latitude; LOC_X -> mtm_x; LOC_Y -> mtm_y;
      DERNIER_STATUT -> last_status; DATE_DERNIER_STATUT -> last_status_at.
    columns:
      - name: contact_sk
        description: >
          Surrogate key, one per source row. md5 of a hash of all raw source columns plus a row
          number within each group of identical rows, so it is deterministic across runs and
          distinct even for exact duplicates.
        data_tests:
          - unique
          - not_null
      - name: request_id
        description: >
          Request identifier (source ID_UNIQUE), e.g. '22-105694-A'. Null for all 'Information'
          contacts. Unique among non-null values.
      - name: request_base_id
        description: request_id with any trailing '-A'/'-B' letter suffix removed. Null when request_id is null.
      - name: request_id_suffix
        description: The single letter after the final hyphen of request_id (e.g. 'A'), or null if there is none.
      - name: is_unexpected_id_prefix
        description: True when request_id starts with '20-' or '21-', which is unexpected because all contacts were created in 2022 or later.
      - name: contact_nature
        description: >
          Kind of contact (source NATURE): Requete (service request), Information, Plainte
          (complaint) or Commentaire (comment).
      - name: activity_name
        description: Service or topic the contact is about (source ACTI_NOM), French text. Known casing variants are unified.
      - name: created_at
        description: When the contact was created (source DDS_DATE_CREATION). Montreal local time, no timezone.
      - name: last_status_at
        description: When the status last changed (source DATE_DERNIER_STATUT). Montreal local time, no timezone. Equals created_at for contacts never updated.
      - name: last_status
        description: Most recent status of the contact, French text (e.g. Terminée, Refusée, Prise en charge). Null for 'Information' contacts.
        data_tests:
          # Every status in the data must exist in the status_mapping seed. A new, unmapped
          # status fails here, so it cannot silently be treated as open downstream.
          # (relationships ignores nulls, so Information contacts are fine.)
          - relationships:
              arguments:
                to: ref('status_mapping')
                field: status
      - name: original_channel
        description: Channel through which the contact originally arrived (source PROVENANCE_ORIGINALE), e.g. Téléphone, Mobile, Courriel.
      - name: phone_contact_count
        description: Number of times this request was reported by telephone (source PROVENANCE_TELEPHONE). A count, not a 0/1 flag.
      - name: email_contact_count
        description: Number of times reported by email (source PROVENANCE_COURRIEL). A count.
      - name: in_person_contact_count
        description: Number of times reported in person (source PROVENANCE_PERSONNE). A count.
      - name: mail_contact_count
        description: Number of times reported by postal mail (source PROVENANCE_COURRIER). A count.
      - name: fax_contact_count
        description: Number of times reported by fax (source PROVENANCE_TELECOPIEUR). A count.
      - name: council_contact_count
        description: Number of times reported through a municipal body or council (source PROVENANCE_INSTANCE). A count.
      - name: mobile_app_contact_count
        description: Number of times reported through the mobile app (source PROVENANCE_MOBILE). A count.
      - name: social_media_contact_count
        description: Number of times reported through social media (source PROVENANCE_MEDIASOCIAUX). A count.
      - name: website_contact_count
        description: Number of times reported through the website (source PROVENANCE_SITEINTERNET). A count.
      - name: responsible_unit
        description: Parent organizational unit responsible for handling the contact (source UNITE_RESP_PARENT).
      - name: location_type
        description: Kind of location (source TYPE_LIEU_INTERV) - Adresse, Intersection, Troncon (street segment) or Installation (facility). Null for 'Information' contacts.
      - name: street
        description: Street name of the location (source RUE).
      - name: cross_street_1
        description: First cross street for Intersection locations (source RUE_INTERSECTION1).
      - name: cross_street_2
        description: Second cross street for Intersection locations (source RUE_INTERSECTION2).
      - name: postal_code
        description: Postal code, uppercase with no spaces (e.g. 'H2L3A7').
      - name: borough
        description: >
          Borough or reconciled municipality as recorded on the contact (source ARRONDISSEMENT),
          with ' - ' separators standardized to '-' to match borough_geo.
      - name: borough_geo
        description: Borough derived from the geocoded coordinates (source ARRONDISSEMENT_GEO). Same separator format as borough.
      - name: borough_mismatch
        description: True when borough and borough_geo are both present and differ after normalization.
      - name: is_non_borough_value
        description: True when borough is a placeholder rather than a real borough ('Ville de Montréal' or 'Extérieur de Montréal').
      - name: longitude
        description: Longitude in WGS84 degrees (source LOC_LONG).
      - name: latitude
        description: Latitude in WGS84 degrees (source LOC_LAT).
      - name: mtm_x
        description: X coordinate in the projected MTM zone 8 system (source LOC_X).
      - name: mtm_y
        description: Y coordinate in the projected MTM zone 8 system (source LOC_Y).
      - name: has_geocoding_error
        description: True when the city's geographic database flagged a location error (source LOC_ERREUR_GDT = 1).
      - name: is_exact_duplicate
        description: True when the row belongs to a group of rows identical across every source column (all copies are flagged, including the first).
